UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Disable Legacy PME for Root ports Legacy PME are enabled by default in FSP-S UPD. This policy sets PME Interrupt Enable (PIE) bit of RCTL register to trigger interrupt generation when RSTS.PS state has changed (either due to 0->1 transition or due to this bit being set with RSTS.PS already set). Due to this interrupt generation, system wakes from sleep immediately it enters. This patch overrides root port legacy pme upd policy from coreboot to ensure no false SCI is triggerd when system is in S3/S0ix state. BUG=b:113083354 BRANCH=none TEST=Able to make S3 resume using wake on wifi connect/disconnect usecase without any failure. FROMGIT: drm/i915: Apply correct ddi translation table for AML device Amber Lake used the same gen graphics as Kaby Lake. Kernel driver should configure KBL's DDI buffer setting for AML ULX as well. So far, driver would load DDI translation table that used for KBL H/S platform and apply it on AML devices. But AML is belong to ULX series. CHROMIUM: config: Enable softlockup detector on all platforms This config is already enabled on x86 platforms, but it isn't enabled on arm64 or arm platforms. Enable it in the common config so that we can detect softlockups on the all architectures and make the system panic if this happens too. This matches how the v4.4 kernel works. This is this script: cat << EOF | tee -a chromeos/config/arm64/common.config chromeos/config/armel/common.config CONFIG_BOOTPARAM_SOFTLOCKUP_PANIC=y CONFIG_BOOTPARAM_SOFTLOCKUP_PANIC_VALUE=1 CONFIG_SOFTLOCKUP_DETECTOR=y EOF ./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig olddefconfig on top of a normalized config. BUG=None TEST=Build and boot kernel, modprobe configs && check for softlockup config enabled here Change-Id: I05451110d965c4b84f83d307920881087d632d7c Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <swboyd@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1264256 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

arc-setup: Do not abort when arcbootcontinue command failed As mentioned in the code comment, the command fails when it is executed after the container is shut down (or in the middle of its shutdown or crash.) The command can fail, for example, if the Chrome browser process crashes right after sign in, or if Chrome browser restarts the container under severe OOM conditions. Since the command failure is not something we can directly fix, uploading arc-setup crash reports to the crash server is not something actionable. It only confuses people looking at crash/. This CL stops sending such reports, and instead just leave logs in /var/log/arc.log. BUG=b:80499056 TEST=ARC still works Change-Id: Icade3e710821a072913289c3ba2a2e083a21c7e3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1266610 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Yusuke Sato <yusukes@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hidehiko Abe <hidehiko@chromium.org>
